import markdown

# Check if the current name contains footnote numbers
md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=["toc", "footnotes"])
source = "# Multi[^1] and[^2] refs\n\n[^1]: first\n[^2]: second\n"
result = md.convert(source)

name = md.toc_tokens[0]["name"]
print(f"Name: {name!r}")
print(f"Contains '1': {'1' in name}")
print(f"Contains '2': {'2' in name}")

raw_message.reasoning:
Interesting! The current code produces name = "Multi1 and2 refs" - it includes the footnote numbers but not the markers. This is because get_name extracts text content from the element, which includes the text "1" and "2" from inside the sup elements.

After m2, with run_postprocessors, the footnotes postprocessor would replace the footnote references with something else (or remove them), so the heading content passed to striptags wouldn't have those numbers.

This is a behavioral difference I can test for! Let me verify:
